_about: Every Pixelforge game ever played. AI games read their scores from C:/Users/yentl/pixelforge-arena/games/<id>/result.json; human games are entered here by hand. Run `python arena/collect.py` after adding a game. Each round lists its tasks; every game's clicks (and a human's seconds) has one number per task.

r1.name: Round 1
r1.note: No coach yet: every AI played alone. Yentl's run had hints from Claude on task 2.

r2.name: Round 2
r2.note: Level 2, still no coach. Yentl played without hints, on the first version, where a cookie bug cost a few extra clicks on task 4 (fixed before the AIs played).

r3.name: Round 3
r3.note: Same Level 2, but the AIs got no text at all: only screenshots, and they clicked on pixel positions like a mouse. Still no coach. Yentl's Level 2 score (64 clicks) is in Round 2.

r4.name: Round 4
r4.note: Same as Round 3, but the AIs could ask a rule-based teacher for the next step. Haiku asked once; Luna never asked. One game each, so differences of a few clicks or a minute are within normal variation.

r5.name: Round 5
r5.note: Level 3: an open case with 10 discoveries (the last 3 come from the final report). Screen only, 150 commands, no teacher.

r6.name: Round 6
r6.note: Same as Round 5, but the AIs could ask the rule-based teacher, which points to the next missing clue and explains the method without giving answers.

r7.name: Round 7
r7.case: Level 4, screen only, 60 commands, no teacher
r7.note: Much harder case: a fake suspect, clues that only line up across three different clocks, AI traps (hidden instructions in the evidence) and only 60 commands.

r8.name: Round 8
r8.case: Level 4, screen only, 60 commands, with teacher
r8.note: Same as Round 7, but the AIs could ask the rule-based teacher. Every question costs one of the 60 commands.

r9.name: Round 9
r9.case: Level 4, screen only, 60 commands, teacher questions free
r9.note: Same as Round 8, but asking the teacher no longer uses a command (max 20 questions).
